$comment: Manifest of Dice UI components to port to shadcn-svelte. EXECUTION ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER. 'wave' is advisory metadata only. Edit freely; port-components.ps1 -DryRun validates this file.

components.name: Direction Provider
components.notes: RTL/LTR context consumed by marquee, scroller, masonry, sortable, kanban, segmented-input, combobox and others. Port first so every later component can read the existing direction context instead of inventing one.
components.promptExtra: This is a context-only utility: no visual output. Expose a `<DirectionProvider dir="ltr|rtl">` wrapper plus a `useDirection()`-equivalent reader that falls back to the nearest DOM `dir` attribute when no provider is present, exactly like upstream. The reader must be safe to call outside a provider.

components.name: Pending
components.notes: Pending/loading state wrapper consumed by action-bar, file-upload, editable and every async-action surface. Upstream uses React's useTransition/useFormStatus; the Svelte port must express the same states without React-specific hooks.
components.promptExtra: React's `useFormStatus` and `useTransition` have no Svelte equivalent. Model the pending state explicitly: an optional `pending` prop for controlled use, plus an internal derived state driven by an async action handler. Document this divergence in the spec's Assumptions section.

components.name: Status
components.notes: Simplest component in the set. This is the reference implementation for file layout, barrel shape, demo route and test style. Get it right before anything else.
components.promptExtra: This component is the CONVENTION SETTER for the whole project. Be deliberate about the directory layout, the index.ts barrel shape, the tv()/cn() variant style, the data-* attribute naming and the vitest file structure: every later component will be told to copy it.

components.name: Stat
components.notes: Compound presentational component (root/label/value/delta). Establishes the multi-part namespace-import convention.

components.name: Swap
components.notes: Two-state crossfade/rotate transition between children. First component to need Svelte transitions and prefers-reduced-motion handling.
components.promptExtra: Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: when the user has requested reduced motion, swap instantly instead of animating. Add a test asserting this.

components.name: Color Swatch
components.notes: Colour parsing/normalisation helpers here are reused by color-picker in wave 3. Put them in a shared module, not inline.
components.promptExtra: Any colour parsing/conversion helper must live in its own exported module so `color-picker` (wave 3) can import it rather than duplicating it.

components.name: Circular Progress
components.notes: SVG arc maths shared with gauge. Determinate and indeterminate modes, role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max.
components.promptExtra: Accessibility is the point here: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax when determinate, and no aria-valuenow when indeterminate. Test both.

components.name: Gauge
components.notes: Shares SVG arc geometry with circular-progress; reuse that module rather than recomputing.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the arc-geometry helper written for `circular-progress` instead of duplicating the maths. If it is not exported yet, export it from there and import it here.

components.name: Badge Overflow
components.notes: ResizeObserver-driven measurement of how many badges fit, with a +N overflow indicator. Consumed later by data-table facets.
components.promptExtra: The measurement loop must be a ResizeObserver in a `$effect` with a proper teardown, never a resize event listener. Guard against SSR: no DOM access during server render.

components.name: Timeline
components.notes: Ordered list semantics with horizontal and vertical orientations.
components.promptExtra: Use real list semantics (ol/li) so screen readers announce position and count. Support both orientations, including RTL for the horizontal one.

components.name: Marquee
components.notes: First real consumer of the direction context - validates wave 0 early.
components.promptExtra: Read the existing direction context from the ported `direction-provider` rather than adding a local `dir` prop only. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by pausing the animation. Pause on hover/focus must be keyboard reachable.

components.name: Scroller
components.notes: Overflow detection plus scroll-affordance buttons/shadows. Its scroll utilities are reused by scroll-spy and tour.
components.promptExtra: Extract the scroll-position/overflow detection into a reusable `.svelte.ts` module: `scroll-spy` and `tour` (wave 3) will be told to import it.

components.name: Masonry
components.notes: Responsive column layout with linear or balanced packing, plus a CSS-columns fallback path.
components.promptExtra: Preserve upstream's SSR-safe fallback: the first server-rendered paint must not depend on measurement. Support RTL column ordering via the direction context.

components.name: Banner
components.notes: Dismissible announcement bar. First component with controlled/uncontrolled open state - establishes that pattern for the whole project.
components.promptExtra: This component establishes the CONTROLLED/UNCONTROLLED pattern for the project: a `$bindable` `open` prop with an internal default, plus an `onOpenChange` callback that fires in both modes. Later components will copy it, so make it exemplary and test both modes.

components.name: Relative Time Card
components.notes: First hover-card composition. Live-updating relative timestamps via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.
components.promptExtra: Use `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; never ship a bespoke formatter. The live-update interval must be cleared in the `$effect` teardown. Tests must pin the clock (fake timers) rather than sleeping.

components.name: Speed Dial
components.notes: Upstream ships a test file - port its assertions too. Radial/linear expanding action menu with roving focus.
components.promptExtra: Upstream has a test file at .reference/diceui/docs/registry/bases/radix/test/speed-dial.test.tsx. Read it and port every assertion it makes to vitest + @testing-library/svelte, in addition to your own tests.

components.name: Checkbox Group
components.notes: First form primitive. Establishes the Field / data-invalid / form-integration conventions from rules/forms.md for the whole of wave 2. Upstream also has a standalone package with more complete behaviour - read both.
components.promptExtra: This component establishes the FORM conventions for the project: hidden native inputs for form submission, `name`/`required`/`disabled` propagation, validation state exposed as `data-invalid`, and label/description/error wiring via aria-describedby. Follow .agents/skills/shadcn-svelte/rules/forms.md exactly; later form components will copy this.

components.name: Segmented Input
components.notes: Multi-segment input (OTP-like) with per-segment focus movement. Its segment-navigation logic is reused by time-picker.
components.promptExtra: Extract the segment focus-navigation logic into a reusable module: `time-picker` will be told to import it. Paste of a full value must distribute across segments. Arrow-key navigation must respect the direction context.

components.name: Mask Input
components.notes: The formatting engine here is the dependency of phone-input. Upstream ships a test file - port its assertions.
components.promptExtra: Upstream has a test file at .reference/diceui/docs/registry/bases/radix/test/mask-input.test.tsx - read it and port every assertion. The mask/format engine must be a standalone exported module because `phone-input` will import it. Caret position after programmatic reformatting is the hard part: test it explicitly.

components.name: Phone Input
components.notes: Country selector plus masked national number. Reuses the mask-input formatting engine.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the formatting engine exported by `mask-input` rather than reimplementing it. Match upstream's dependency choice for country metadata exactly - do not substitute a different phone library.

components.name: Time Picker
components.notes: Hour/minute/second/period segments with 12h and 24h modes. Reuses segmented-input navigation.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the segment-navigation module exported by `segmented-input`. Locale-aware 12h/24h detection must go through Intl, not a hard-coded list. Test wrap-around at boundaries (23 -> 00) and the AM/PM segment.

components.name: Tags Input
components.notes: Upstream also has a standalone package with the fuller implementation - read both. Consumed by key-value.
components.promptExtra: Read BOTH the registry component and .reference/diceui/packages/tags-input (the standalone package has the more complete behaviour: keyboard editing, paste splitting, duplicate/max handling, blur behaviour). Port the union of the two.

components.name: Editable
components.notes: Click-to-edit inline field with submit/cancel. Upstream ships a test file. Consumed by key-value.
components.promptExtra: Upstream has a test file at .reference/diceui/docs/registry/bases/radix/test/editable.test.tsx - port every assertion. Focus management is the crux: entering edit mode focuses and selects, Escape cancels and restores focus to the trigger, Enter submits. Test all three.

components.name: Key Value
components.notes: Editable key/value pair list. Composes editable and the tags-input interaction model.
components.promptExtra: Compose the already-ported `editable` component rather than reimplementing inline editing. Duplicate-key handling and row add/remove focus management must be specified and tested.

components.name: QR Code
components.notes: SVG/canvas QR rendering with error-correction levels and an optional overlay.
components.promptExtra: Use the same QR encoding dependency as upstream; do not substitute another library and do not hand-roll the encoder. The rendered output needs an accessible name describing the encoded value.

components.name: Combobox
components.notes: Hardest primitive of the set and a dependency of data-table. Upstream has both a registry component and a standalone package - read both.
components.promptExtra: This is the most important component in wave 3: `data-table` depends on it. Read the standalone package at .reference/diceui/packages/combobox as well as the registry component - the package has the complete keyboard and filtering semantics. Full APG combobox pattern: aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant, role=listbox/option, typeahead, Home/End/PageUp/PageDown, single and multiple selection, creatable entries. Every one of those needs a test.

components.name: Responsive Dialog
components.notes: Dialog on desktop, drawer on mobile, behind one API. Establishes the media-query rune used by later responsive components.
components.promptExtra: Port `use-mobile.ts` as a reusable `.svelte.ts` media-query rune first, then build on it. Switching breakpoint while open must not lose state or trap focus in a detached node - test that transition explicitly.

components.name: Action Bar
components.notes: Floating contextual action bar. Shares its floating/portal mechanics with selection-toolbar, which follows immediately.
components.promptExtra: Extract the floating-container mechanics (portal, positioning, enter/exit transition, focus containment) into a reusable module: `selection-toolbar` is ported next and will be told to import it.

components.name: Selection Toolbar
components.notes: Text-selection-anchored floating toolbar. Reuses action-bar's floating mechanics.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the floating-container module exported by `action-bar`. Selection tracking must use the Selection API with a teardown, and must not fight the browser's own selection on touch.

components.name: Scroll Spy
components.notes: IntersectionObserver-driven active-section tracking. Upstream ships a test file. Its observer utilities are reused by tour.
components.promptExtra: Upstream has a test file at .reference/diceui/docs/registry/bases/radix/test/scroll-spy.test.tsx - port every assertion. Use IntersectionObserver in a `$effect` with teardown, and reuse the scroll utilities exported by `scroller`. Extract the observer wrapper so `tour` can import it.

components.name: Stepper
components.notes: Multi-step flow with linear/non-linear modes and validation gating. Upstream ships a test file.
components.promptExtra: Upstream has a test file at .reference/diceui/docs/registry/bases/radix/test/stepper.test.tsx - port every assertion. Controlled and uncontrolled step state, linear vs non-linear navigation, and the roving-focus/aria-current semantics all need tests.

components.name: Tour
components.notes: Guided product tour: spotlight overlay, target anchoring, scroll-into-view, step navigation, focus trapping.
components.promptExtra: Focus management is the hardest part: each step must trap focus in the tour popover, restore focus on exit, and remain escapable. Scroll-into-view must honour prefers-reduced-motion. Reuse the observer wrapper from `scroll-spy`.

components.name: Color Picker
components.notes: Saturation area, hue/alpha sliders, format switching (hex/rgb/hsl). Reuses the colour helpers from color-swatch.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the colour parsing/conversion module exported by `color-swatch`. The saturation area must be operable by keyboard (arrow keys, with a larger step under Shift) and expose role=slider semantics with aria-valuetext - this is where most colour pickers fail accessibility. Test it.

components.name: File Upload
components.notes: Drag-and-drop dropzone, file list, per-file progress, validation, accept/max-size/max-files.
components.promptExtra: The dropzone must be fully keyboard operable (a real focusable control that opens the file dialog), not drag-only. Do not port upstream's uploadthing wiring - the upload transport stays consumer-supplied via a callback. State that in the spec's Assumptions.

components.name: Media Player
components.notes: Largest single component outside data-table: controls, seek bar, volume, captions, fullscreen, PiP, keyboard shortcuts.
components.promptExtra: Bind to the media element with Svelte's native media bindings (bind:currentTime, bind:paused, bind:duration, bind:volume, bind:muted) instead of manual event listeners wherever possible. Every documented keyboard shortcut needs a test. Captions/track support must not be dropped.

components.name: Sortable
components.notes: Drag-and-drop reordering. Its pointer/keyboard DnD abstraction is reused by kanban, which is ported next.
components.promptExtra: Upstream builds on dnd-kit, which is React-only. Decide the Svelte strategy explicitly in the plan (a Svelte DnD library vs a bespoke pointer/keyboard implementation) and justify it. Keyboard-accessible reordering (grab with Space/Enter, move with arrows, drop with Space, cancel with Escape) plus aria-live announcements are MANDATORY, not optional. Extract the DnD core into a reusable `.svelte.ts` module: `kanban` is next and will import it.

components.name: Kanban
components.notes: Multi-column board: cross-column drag, column reordering. Reuses sortable's DnD core.
components.promptExtra: Reuse the DnD core module exported by `sortable` - do not write a second drag implementation. Cross-column keyboard movement and its aria-live announcements need tests.

components.name: Data Table
components.notes: Highest fan-in component, ported last so every dependency is a real file on disk. Built on TanStack Table.
components.promptExtra: Use @tanstack/table-core via its Svelte adapter - the headless core is framework-agnostic, so column defs, sorting, filtering, pagination and row selection port almost directly. Compose the already-ported `combobox`, `badge-overflow`, `checkbox-group` and `sortable` for the filter, facet, selection and column-reorder surfaces instead of reimplementing them. This is a LARGE component: expect the plan to schedule the toolbar, column header, faceted filter, date filter, slider filter, pagination, view options and skeleton as separate subcomponents, mirroring upstream's file split.
